children: The equity benchmark indices traded lower on Monday as sentiment ​remained subdued over elevated crude ‌oil prices and their impact on inflation, while selling in IT shares also dented market sentiments.
At around 9:45 a.m., the Sensex was down 521.64 points or 0.71 percent at 72,602.19, while the broader Nifty declined to 22,422.60, down 177.40 points or 0.78 percent.

: IT stocks shed 2.3%, leading the ‌losses. ⁠Infosys lost 3.4% after it slashed its annual revenue growth forecast as weakness in its key North American ​market outweighed ​its ⁠higher-than-expected revenue.

: Brent crude futures traded around $114 a barrel, easing ​from a near six-month high ​of $117 ⁠after the Indian market close on Friday, though ongoing attacks on Saudi ⁠Arabia ​kept supply concerns in ​focus.
: Investors are also focused on the US Federal ​Reserve's policy decision this ​week.

Ponmudi R, CEO of Enrich Money, a SEBI-registered online trading and wealth-tech firm, said "Nifty 50 continues to remain under selling pressure, with the 22,750–22,800 zone acting as an immediate resistance band and attracting persistent selling interest. A sustained breakout above this range could help stabilise the index, ease near-term selling pressure and pave the way for a recovery towards the psychological 23,000 mark."

"On the downside, immediate support is placed at 22,400–22,300. A decisive breakdown below this zone could intensify selling pressure and expose the index to further downside towards 22,200–22,000. The index maintains a cautious-to-bearish outlook, with a sustained move above 22,800 required to improve recovery prospects, while a breakdown below the immediate support zone could accelerate the decline," he added.

title: Sensex falls 500 pts, Nifty below 22,450: Selling in IT shares among key factors behind market decline
